correctness.rationale: The universal three-indicator raw-moment identities and common full-extinction event establish exact delta-third=3(1-mu)delta-variance under common exchangeable primary losses. An exhaustive census of all 387 connected no-isolate binary bipartite incidence matrices with at most six vertices, partitioned into 44 fixed bidegree signatures, gives identical full fixed-k conditional laws within signatures. The delivered self-contained executable checker reproduces this census, the two seven-vertex connected trees, exact bidegrees, polynomial identities, and four rational probability checks. The variance gap is strictly positive and the cubic crossing is unique for 0<q<1. No unbounded extension is inferred from finite checks.

originality.rationale: Full primary texts of Memmott et al. (2004), Burgos et al. (2006) and Jones et al. (2024) substantiate the baseline loss model and mean robustness, but not the new structural third-central-moment law combined with sharp seven-vertex bidegree-matched threshold. Exact implication comparisons show that prior mean results do not fix overlap-dependent second or third moments. The elementary algebraic moment expansion is not itself claimed novel; the exact bidegree-sharp coextinction consequence is. Possibility of a stronger unlocated reliability/cumulant theorem remains.
residual_risks: An unlocated specialized graph-reliability cumulant result might imply or explicitly state the same three-plant identity or sharp small-network comparison.
Published mean-robustness methods could be extendable to this moment result, but such an extension was not stated or established in the inspected papers.

value.rationale: Among fixed-size networks matched on both guild degree sequences and on all single-plant extinction probabilities, the result supplies the first possible network size at which a natural distribution-asymmetry statistic reverses order with primary-loss probability despite a fixed variance order. The universal identity isolates the structural mechanism at mean secondary loss crossing one. This provides a motivated exact benchmark distinct from routine recomputation of expected robustness or a random slice of tiny networks.
